summary: A 2005 lighthouse-style building on Cunningham Key in Tierra Verde, Florida, where the Coast Guard permits a private aid to navigation, run by Tampa Bay Watch.

structures.note: Rises 74 feet, per Tampa Bay Watch. The apparent lantern is an atrium inside the education center.

access.note: Access is tied to Tampa Bay Watch programs, events and facility policies.

visit.note: No public tower-climbing program. A Lighthouse Passport book can be bought and stamped at the Tierra Verde education center.

facts.agency: Tampa Bay Watch (manages the site under an agreement with Pinellas County and the State of Florida)

Coast Guard installed an optic classified as a private aid to navigation; the Florida Lighthouse Association gives no separate date and places it with the building's 2005 entry into service
Tierra Verde Marine Education Center renamed Auer Marine Education Center

notes_for_editor: Thin station: three readable sources, all but the photo blog written by or for the operator or a faux-lighthouse directory. No keepers, no wrecks, no storms are sourced, and the light has no keeper history (a 2005 privately maintained aid); the story has no chapter headings for that reason. No USLHS match: the roster lookup offered only 'Tampa Bay Beacons', a USLHS place marked 'not existing' whose keepers (1895-1948) belong to a different place; it was not used. Not cited, because paywalled: two Tampa Bay Times articles of 24 and 30 November 2005 ('New marine and education center, new beacon for seeker of safe harbor'; 'Marine center ready to teach'). Their search snippets say the $1.8-million center opened 3 December 2005 and the light was the first lighthouse built in Florida since 1954; a person with archive access should check these before the story uses them. Coordinates differ slightly: record 27.654705, -82.717913 (OSM way centroid); Florida Lighthouse Association 27.6548394, -82.720024; ARLHS USA-1335 27.65454, -82.71767 (ARLHS says not for navigation). The offset is about 0.2 km; left as is. Height: the record's structure height is 13.0 m, while Tampa Bay Watch says 74 feet (about 22.6 m); the record's focal height of 23 m is not in any source read here and is left out of the facts. The record's 'Fl W 4s' is not stated in any source read here (Tampa Bay Watch gives a quarter-second flash every four seconds and no colour); verify on the USCG Light List before publishing a characteristic. The record's photo (Gasparilla_Island_SP_lighthouse02.jpg) is titled for another place and should not be used for this light without a check. Scope: this is a lighthouse-style building that does serve as a private aid to navigation, so it stays in scope; the Florida Lighthouse Association's 'faux lighthouse' label is noted in the story.
